classification.difficultyReason: Identify different ownership and age intervals, recover their endpoint values, and divide each loss by the correct number of years.

content.prompt: Ms Wu’s seven-year-old car is worth $\$5600$, and has been depreciating at 22.5% p.a. Calculate your answers to the nearest dollar.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How much was it worth four years ago?

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Value four years ago}&=5600\div0.775^4\\\text{Value four years ago}&\approx\$15\,523\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: How much was it worth seven years ago?

children.label: c
children.prompt: Ms Wu, however, only bought the car four years ago, at its depreciated value at that time. What has been Ms Wu’s average depreciation in dollars per year over the four years she has owned the car?

answer.worked:
Use the unrounded value when Ms Wu bought the car.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Average annual depreciation}&=\frac{5600\div0.775^4-5600}{4}\\\text{Average annual depreciation}&\approx\$2481\text{ per year}\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: What was the average depreciation in dollars per year over the first three years of the car’s life?

answer.short:
$\$5942$ per year.

Use the loss from new to age three, divided by three.
answer.worked:
Four years ago the car was three years old. Use unrounded endpoint values.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Loss in first three years}&=5600\div0.775^7-5600\div0.775^4\\\text{Average annual depreciation}&=\frac{5600\div0.775^7-5600\div0.775^4}{3}\\\text{Average annual depreciation}&\approx\$5942\text{ per year}\end{align*}$$
